🕌 Halal Guide

Halal Food in China

Muslim Traveler's Guide – halal restaurants, Muslim Quarter in Xi'an, historic mosques you can visit

🕌 Muslim Guide⏱️ 8 min read
Home◂Tourism in China◂Halal Food

Many Muslim travelers ask: Can you find halal food in China? The answer is definitely yes. China is home to more than 23 million Muslims and contains more than 35,000 mosques. In major cities you'll find diverse halal restaurants, and in some cities like Xi'an there are complete Islamic neighborhoods. Arcadia Tourism ensures halal restaurants are available at every stop within its travel programs.

Muslim Quarter in Xi'an 🕌

The Muslim Quarter in Xi'an is the most famous Islamic neighborhood in all of China. It has streets packed with halal restaurants and traditional markets. The cuisine here is unique, mixing Chinese and Islamic flavors – from grilled lamb to hand-pulled noodles. The neighborhood also contains the historic Great Mosque dating back more than a thousand years (read about it in Tourist Attractions).

Halal Restaurants in Beijing 🍖

In Beijing you'll find halal restaurants in the Niujie (Ox Street) area – Beijing's oldest Islamic neighborhood, featuring the historic Niujie Mosque dating back to the 10th century AD. Halal restaurants are also available in tourist areas such as Wangfujing and Sanlitun.

Halal in Shanghai and Guangzhou 🥘

In Shanghai halal restaurants are available in various areas, most notably around Shanghai Mosque in the Huangpu district. In Guangzhou – the main destination for business tourism – good halal options are available, especially around the Canton Fair area.

Chinese Halal Cuisine 🍜

Chinese halal cuisine is rich and diverse. Among the most famous dishes: Lanzhou Lamian (Lanzhou hand-pulled noodles), Yangrouchuan (grilled lamb skewers), Dapanji (chicken cooked with spices), and Niurou Mian (beef noodle soup).

Historic Mosques to Visit 🕋

China contains remarkable historic mosques: Great Mosque of Xi'an (742 AD), Niujie Mosque in Beijing (996 AD), Huaisheng Mosque in Guangzhou (China's oldest mosque dating to the 7th century), and Dongsi Mosque in Beijing. These mosques uniquely blend traditional Chinese architecture with Islamic art.

💡 Arcadia Tip for Muslim Travelers

Look for the characters 清真 (Qingzhen) on restaurant storefronts – it means "halal" in Chinese. You can also use apps like HalalTrip to find the nearest halal restaurant. At Arcadia we guarantee halal restaurants are available every day of the travel program. Also check general travel tips.
